claim_tested: WSS/profile misfit ratio scales as alpha^2
verdict: MECHANISM CONFIRMED; asymptotic exponent is -3/2 (derived and verified), not -2. Physiological window is transitional at ~-1.8.

wss_misfit_saturates.mechanism: normalised wall-shear transfer functions tend to 1/alpha (channel) and 2/alpha (pipe); ratio exactly 2, verified to 4 digits at alpha=300

note: These are EXACT analytic reference values, not measurements, so the departure from -2 is signal rather than noise. The two-point estimate at alpha 10 and 20 gives 3.53 where alpha^2 predicts 4.00.
what_survives: The mechanism claim is unaffected and is the strong part: profile misfit DECAYS while WSS misfit SATURATES at exactly 0.5, so they scale in opposite directions. A uniformly more sensitive quantity cannot do that. Quote the exponent as ~alpha^1.8 over the physiological window, or avoid a power law and quote the ratio at the operating point (53x at alpha=10, 190x at alpha=20).
numerical_limit: the J0 kernel overflows for alpha >~ 1000 (complex Bessel argument); not a physics limit

asymptotic_law_DERIVED.prediction: profile amplitude misfit ~ alpha^(-3/2), from the Stokes-layer curvature correction
asymptotic_law_DERIVED.mechanism: at large alpha the channel kernel is a pure exponential while the pipe carries an extra sqrt(a/r) from J0(z) ~ sqrt(2/pi z) cos(z - pi/4). The pointwise difference is therefore [(a-r)/2a] exp(-(a-r)/delta): linear growth away from the wall, killed exponentially at the layer edge. Two factors of alpha^(-1/2) follow - the amplitude difference is O(delta/a), and the layer occupies only O(1/alpha) of the cross-section so the L2 norm picks up another sqrt(1/alpha).
asymptotic_law_DERIVED.prefactor_note: the closed form gives 0.25*2^0.75 = 0.4204 for |chan - pipe|; the metric is the AMPLITUDE misfit ||chan|-|pipe||, which retains only the projection along the unperturbed vector, hence the factor ~0.48
asymptotic_law_DERIVED.numerics: requires exponentially-scaled kernels (scipy jve, and cosh written as exp(K(y-1))) - the naive forms overflow above alpha ~ 1000
asymptotic_law_DERIVED.consequence: the honest law is ratio ~ alpha^(3/2) asymptotically, with the PHYSIOLOGICAL window alpha 10-20 sitting in transition at ~alpha^1.8. The transition is now explained rather than fitted.

projection_factor.why: the metric is the AMPLITUDE misfit ||u_p|-|u_c||, not |u_p-u_c|, so it retains only Re(d conj(u_c))/|u_c| - the projection of the perturbation onto the unperturbed vector
projection_factor.integral: sqrt( int_0^inf s^2 (e^-s cos s - e^-2s)^2 / (1 - 2 e^-s cos s + e^-2s) ds ) / sqrt( int_0^inf s^2 e^-2s ds )

closed_form_prefactor.extrapolation: prefactor(alpha) = p_inf + c/alpha fitted over alpha = 200..3200 (0.204248, 0.203007, 0.202395, 0.202091, 0.201940); the finite-alpha correction is O(1/alpha)
closed_form_prefactor.method_note: Fitting p_inf + c/alpha and extrapolating IS Richardson extrapolation - the same operation as fitting an observed order in mesh spacing, which is where this programme started. A 0.3% gap at finite alpha is a truncation error like any other; treating it as one closed the last decimal. Note also the evidential status: most scaling-law claims show a log-log plot and quote a slope. Four-digit agreement between a fully DERIVED prefactor and an extrapolated measurement is a different category - it says the mechanism is understood, not merely that the trend is right, and it is what makes 'a wrong governing solution passes profile validation' a derived result rather than an observation.

asymptotic_law_DERIVED.status: COMPLETE - exponent, prefactor and metric projection all derived; nothing absorbed as residual
